lots.guide_summary: Close entries run AUD 260 to 1,000, all SOLD at Australian rooms in 2026 (For-Auction matched set 260, McCann sets for six 400, 700 and 1,000; the 400 and 700 are the same set). Wider guide AUD 183 to 1,818 adds two older overseas SOLD results (Waddington's 2023, Gorringes 2022 Kinkozan). Three dealer ASKING prices in Europe run AUD 484 to 1,290 and are not prices paid. No UNSOLD found. Rates: GBP 1 = AUD 1.914, CAD 1 = AUD 1.016, EUR 1 = AUD 1.613 (19 Oct 2026, current rates applied to old sales).
lots.working: No exact same-item sale exists (lot 162 is a part set with a chipped saucer). SOLD close entries in the last 24 months: AUD 260 (matched part set, Feb 2026), 400, 700 and 1,000 (full sets for six, 2026). Using the lowest, as a part set should not beat a complete set: keep_max_hammer = 260 / 1.22 = 213.1, rounded down to $210 (all-in $256.20). flip: likely resale A$260 (lowest close SOLD), less eBay AU final value fee 13.4% (A$34.84) and A$0.30 order fee, less A$30 packed fragile outbound postage = A$194.86; / 2.44 = 79.9, rounded down to $75. Armitage premium 22% incl GST; inbound freight $0 (pickup 9 Goodman Crt, Invermay). Whether the McCann and For-Auction figures include premium is not stated, so they may understate buyer cost.
lots.confidence_reason: Mark read in the photos (光山) and four Australian 2026 SOLD pages opened, but none is the same item: they are full or matched sets, and the maker behind the Kozan mark is not confirmed.
lots.condition: Small rim chip on one saucer (visible in photo 4, left rim). Light gilt wear possible. No visible cracks in the photos but bases of the teapot, sugar and jug are not shown. One cup short of the saucers.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 1 shows 10 pieces: teapot, sugar, milk jug, 3 cups on saucers and a saucer on a plate stand. Photo 5 enlarged: rectangular gold-on-black cartouche reading 光山 (Kozan). Painting is fine, with raised gilt bamboo on cups and saucers. Photo 4 crop: white rim chip on a saucer.
lots.question_for_armitage: Please confirm the piece count (10?) and whether any piece other than the one saucer is chipped, cracked or restored, especially the teapot spout, lids and finials. Are the teapot, sugar and jug marked with the same 光山 cartouche?
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped: (1) Bonhams Edinburgh 2005 GBP 411.25: snippet only, Bonhams returns 403, and 21 years old. (2) Chairish USD 2,800: four different pieces (pitcher, tea caddy, one cup), porcelain, US retail fantasy price, not comparable. (3) Gowans 391971 Satsuma vase $320, 430870 vase with cloisonne $120, 365482 cracked vase $40, 377670 Hotei figure $21 and 395238 mixed Satsuma trinkets $15: all re-checked in the Gowans API (prices and dates match), but none is tea ware, so not the same item; local Satsuma demand note only. (4) Gowans 380521 part Japanese coffee set $5: confirmed in API, but a mass-produced damaged moriage set, not comparable in quality. No mislabelled kinds found; the two Appraisily-sourced lots were upgraded from snippet only to page opened after the Invaluable pages loaded for me.

lots.guide_summary: Collection-level close entries run AUD 40 to 560: SOLD AUD 40 to 375 in the last 24 months (Gowans tubs and bags 45 to 190, Leski and Status accumulations 140 to 375, Status album with the same B.D.V. Who's Who and Wills Animals sets 300) and AUD 400 to 700 at Noble in 2010 to 2017; UNSOLD openings AUD 80 to 375, including a 680-card Wills Australian lot that failed three times at 80 to 150. Single-series set lots (category guide) run AUD 25 to 500 and scarce early football outliers 700 to 1,000. No ASKING evidence. All AUD, no conversion.
lots.working: No exact same item exists; the comparison is collection-level accumulations of Australian-issue sets and part sets at Australian rooms in the last 24 months: Leski 451 A$180 (Oct 2026), Leski 1484 A$200 (Mar 2026), Leski 7 A$280 (Oct 2026), Status 20293 A$300 (Mar 2026), Status 20479 A$300 (Nov 2024), Leski 6 A$320, Status 10837 A$375. Smaller Gowans tubs (A$45 to 130) are much smaller than lot 182 and were not used for the floor. keep_max_hammer = 180 / 1.22 = 147.5, rounded down to $145 (all-in $176.90). Caution: Status's 680-card Wills lot with the same Animals and Wild Animal Heads sets failed at A$80 to 150 three times. flip: likely resale A$200 (low end of collection SOLD) through a Melbourne specialist auction, less an assumed 20% seller commission incl GST (A$40) and A$25 outbound postage = A$135; / 2.44 = 55.3, rounded down to $55. Armitage premium 22% incl GST; inbound freight $0 (pickup 9 Goodman Crt, Invermay).
lots.confidence_reason: Index sheet read and many collection-level SOLD pages opened, but the bundles' contents, counts and condition cannot be read in the photos, so the real value could sit well below or above the range.
lots.condition: Unknown. Cards are tied in tight rubber bands and string (risk of band marks and toning). Some cards appear sleeved. Index tallies show mostly part sets; only Wills Animals (60), VC Heroes (25) and S&A Warships are marked complete.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 1 crop: two yellow tins with labelled bundles (the right tin holds four long rows packed edge-up, likely 1,000+ cards on its own), a blue tub, a clear box with more bundles, two small card boxes, modern postcards and a car brochure. Photo 2: handwritten index of Australian issues with catalogue codes (Ardath A72-35, Carreras C18-92/93/94, Wills W62 series, S&A S88-13.2 and S88-15, G. Phillips P50.142, P50.145, P50.143B). No Bradman or scarce pre-1915 football issues are listed.
lots.question_for_armitage: Roughly how many cards are there, and are the 1933 B.D.V. Test Cricketers (does it include Bradman) and the Greys and Carreras footballer bundles substantial? Are the cards in fair condition without heavy band marks or creases? Is the index sheet complete for the whole lot?
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped: Leski 6 Oct 2026 lot 454 (A$900, Leski PDF 661 confirms) because it is an advertising poster, not cards. Everything else re-checked: all 20 Gowans records re-fetched (titles, hammer and bids match); 65 of 67 Invaluable pages re-opened with embedded isLotSold, soldAmount and estimate matching the researcher; Leski PDFs 649 and 661 re-read (lots 256 = 160 and 288 = 140 on the house list though Invaluable shows them passed in; 608 = 160; 580 and 293 Unsold); all 9 Noble pages re-opened and match. Status 20306 and Leski 608 pages would not reload past the bot check (608 is confirmed by the Leski PDF; 20306 kept as a lead only). Re-labelled same_item: single-series set lots (VC Heroes, Wills 1933 Footballers, B.D.V. cricketers and so on) moved to category guide, since they price components rather than a collection like lot 182. No kind mislabelled.

So keep_max_hammer = 0 and flip_max_hammer = 0. lots.confidence_reason: Maker name not readable in the photos (inferred from bases, stands and box) and all same-range prices are unverified eBay snippets.
lots.condition: Figures look clean and complete on the stands in the photos; one boxed in blister, others loose. Small parts (swords, spears) appear present on most but cannot be checked; stands look undamaged. No magazines visible.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photos 1 to 4: three grey two-tier stands moulded GAME OF THRONES, 10 figures each, silver patterned round bases typical of the Eaglemoss partwork. Photo 6 crop: black and gold card box with blister, no legible maker text. Characters look like common early issues (Jon Snow, Daenerys, Tyrion, Cersei, White Walker, Khal Drogo and so on).
lots.question_for_armitage: How many figures in total, are any swords or spears broken or missing, and are the stands free of chips? Is there any Eaglemoss or Hero Collector marking under the bases or stands?
